data.narrative:
Altos Labs, a late-stage biotech company founded by Hal Barron, Rick Klausner, and Hans Bishop, has raised $3.0B to date. The valuation assessment draws from a universe of 3 public comparables (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) in the Biotech & Health sector, alongside 8 private peers including Colossal Biosciences, Abridge, and Recursion Pharmaceuticals.

Only one triangulation method proved applicable. Stage-progression analysis, using total capital raised as a proxy baseline, applies a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical of late-stage progression to the $3.0B funding base, yielding $3.6B. Public-comp anchoring was not feasible due to the absence of disclosed revenue for the target company, a common limitation with private firms. Peer-median analysis could not be applied; while 8 same-sector peers exist, none met minimum thresholds for same-stage or valuation-tier clustering needed for reliable benchmarking.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $3.1B to $4.1B, with a median point of $3.6B. Key uncertainties include the company's actual revenue generation (unavailable for private status), the absence of tighter peer-stage clustering for validation, and reliance on a single methodological anchor. Any refinement would require either disclosure of financial performance metrics or identification of additional late-stage biotech comparables with comparable capital deployment and stage progression.
